newsitem.title: USA: Police seek clues to Versace suspect's final days.
newsitem.headline: Police seek clues to Versace suspect's final days.

text.p: U.S. authorities on Friday pieced together details of Andrew Cunanan's final days, hoping evidence left on a Miami Beach houseboat would offer clues to the motives for his alleged cross-country killing rampage.
Investigators said they were looking for evidence that would close the files on the slaying of Italian designer Gianni Versace and four murders in northern U.S. states.
The probe centred on the powder-blue, two-storey houseboat in Miami Beach's affluent Indian Creek neighbourhood where Cunanan spent his last hours before committing suicide.
A police SWAT team found the alleged spree killer late on Wednesday, dressed only in boxer shorts, sprawled on a bed in the master bedroom.
The weapon he used to take his life, found in his lap, was a .40-calibre handgun whose serial numbers matched a weapon stolen from one of his first victims.
"I can confirm that the number matched to the gun we've been looking for," FBI spokesman Mike Fabregas said on Friday.
The houseboat remained under police cordon as agents fanned out in the neighbourhood, trying to determine if anyone helped Cunanan during his last days on the run.
"We're looking for anything and everything that can help us to further this investigation," Fabregas said. "Anything that can lead us to understand what happened here."

Federal authorities said they would search for a link between Cunanan and the owner of the houseboat, identified by local media as Torsten Reineck, a German citizen who owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. German authorities said they believed Reineck was a fugitive they had sought since 1992.
The FBI located the owner in Las Vegas and said he was being cooperative. Harbouring a fugitive is a federal crime.

"The FBI needs to determine whether any calls were made from the residence, whether there was any connection between Cunanan and the owner, were there signs of forced entry," U.S. Attorney's Office spokesman Wilfredo Fernandez said.

Of particular interest was a blue safe measuring about 18 by 15 inches (45 by 38 cm) found in the master bedroom. The FBI obtained a search warrant for the safe, but would not comment on Friday on whether it had been cracked or what might be found in it.
"There is probable cause to believe the safe may contain more evidence related to the five homicides," an FBI affidavit said.

Authorities hoped to find a note or journal to explain the killing spree, but preliminary searches of the houseboat turned up nothing. "We found no notes, no videotape, no testament," FBI agent Paul Philip said.

The Dade County Medical Examiner's Office on Friday declined to reveal if an autopsy had determined whether Cunanan was infected with the AIDS virus or had a brain tumour or other physical defect that might explain his actions.

Media reports indicated Cunanan, who has been described as a chameleon for his ability to disguise himself, was growing a beard, possibly an attempt to change his appearance yet again to elude the nationwide manhunt.

Cunanan, a gay prostitute, was the only suspect in the murder of Versace, who dressed the world's top models, rock musicians and movie stars. He was shot in the head on the steps of his Miami Beach mansion.

Cunanan was on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list of fugitives even before the Versace slaying. He was suspected in the murders of his friend Jeffrey Trail, 28; his former lover David Madson, 33; Lee Miglin, 72; and William Reese, 45.
Authorities met on Friday to determine whether Fernando Carreira, the houseboat caretaker who stumbled upon Cunanan, should get the $45,000 reward offered for his apprehension.
"He was a dangerous man, he could shoot anyone," Carreira said in stating his case. "I didn't know who it is but I caught him."

Police initially said they did not believe his phone call to report a possible burglar, which did not mention Cunanan, merited the reward. A local television poll of viewers found 97 percent thought Carreira should get the money.
